svg.title: Queue, topic and event hub: three ways a broker hands events to readers
svg.desc: Three columns. Queue: senders put messages into one queue; competing receivers each lock a message with peek-lock, process it and complete it, which removes it; a message that fails is abandoned and delivered again, and after the maximum delivery count it moves to the dead-letter queue; each message is processed by one receiver. Topic: a sender publishes to a topic; every subscription gets its own copy of each message, optionally narrowed by a filter rule on message properties; each subscription behaves like a queue with its own lock, delivery count and dead-letter queue; adding a subscriber needs no change at the sender. Event hub: senders append events to partitions of a log; events stay for the retention period whether or not they were read; each consumer group reads every partition from its own position, the offset, and stores a checkpoint; order is kept within a partition; there is no completion of single events and no dead-letter queue, so a reader skips or stops. Below, how each is registered in Dataverse with the Plug-in Registration Tool: Register New Service Endpoint with the connection string of a shared access signature policy that has the Send claim, then designation type Queue, Topic or Event Hub, message format .NET Binary, JSON or XML, and user information sent; then either a step directly on the endpoint, which posts every matching event, or a custom plug-in that calls the notification service with the endpoint ID and decides in code. Steps on these endpoints are asynchronous.
